subject: Dressing-room storage that feels calm
hook: The calmest wardrobe fronts hide their drawers.
ig:
The calmest wardrobe fronts hide their drawers. Here's why internal drawers are worth asking for.

External drawers break up a run of wardrobe doors: extra lines, extra handles, extra things for the eye to land on. Put the drawers inside, behind the doors, and the front becomes one quiet surface.

What you gain:
— a cleaner look with one handle style at one height
— dust-free storage for socks, underwear and accessories
— room for dividers, so small things stop migrating

What to plan for: internal drawers sit slightly back to clear the doors and hinges, so they lose a little depth. Worth it for most bedrooms, but it's something we'd size properly at the design stage rather than guess.

Which would you choose — drawers on show or tucked inside? Tell us in the comments, and save this for your wardrobe plans.
fb:
Small detail, big difference: putting wardrobe drawers inside, behind the doors.

From the room you just see a clean run of doors. Open them and the drawers are there for socks, belts, jewellery — out of the dust and out of sight. The trade-off is a little lost depth, as the drawers sit back to clear the hinges, which we plan for when we design.
